title: Delta: Latency & Unit-Econ Toolkit
body:
Purpose and audience:
This working brief is for GTM (field sellers, solutions engineers, product marketing) to: 1) sharpen concise latency + unit-econ claims, 2) surface the lab proof-lines buyers care about, and 3) give short demo/objection scripts that map to customer scenarios. Not for external distribution yet (internal draft).

Top-line positioning (one-liner):
Redwood reduces per-request latency and per-meaningful-token cost by combining adaptive batching, prefix/KV caching, and model-routing so customers get predictable p95s and 2–3x lower unit cost on production-style workloads.

Target personas and use cases:
- Product/ML engineers building chat assistants (low tail-latency, high concurrency)
- Platform/infra teams buying reserved capacity (predictable throughput, cost control)
- Head of AI/CTO evaluating TCO for search/QA/agents (cost-per-query and SLA)

Core claims (framed for sales) — keep these tight and testable:
- Claim A (Latency delta): "Typical p95 latency drop of ~40–60% vs unmanaged endpoints under user-like burst patterns."
- Claim B (Unit-econ): "Net cost per meaningful token is typically 2x lower after enabling adaptive batching + KV caching compared to unoptimized single-request serving."
- Claim C (Predictability): "Latency variability reduced — p95/p50 ratio improves by ~2x with our routing+fallback policies."

What we mean by "meaningful token":
- Sales language: tokens that contribute to user-visible output (not repeated system prefixes or redundant KG lookups). Unit-econ claims tie to cost-per-meaningful-token rather than raw token counts.

Lab proof-lines (how to validate internally):
- Test harness: 8-node GPU cluster (mix of 2x A100 40G and 6x A10G), model family: Llama-2-13B-like and an instruction-tuned 7B variant, request profile: 60% chat-turns (avg 120 reqs/sec), concurrency spikes to 1k rps for 30s bursts.
- Measurements to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per 1M meaningful tokens, GPU utilization, effective batching size distribution, cache hit rate, fallback events.
- Representative numbers (lab snapshot — use sparingly externally):
  - Redwood (baseline config): p50=85ms, p95=190ms, cost-per-1k-meaningful-tokens=$0.32
  - Competitor-A (default endpoint): p50=140ms, p95=420ms, cost-per-1k-meaningful-tokens=$0.75
  - Notes: numbers vary by model and prompt shapes; always qualify with "typical production chat workload".

Competitive nuance (short notes for SEs):
- Competitor-A: simpler pricing + point latency numbers. Weakness: no adaptive KV caching or multi-tier routing. Wins on raw model access breadth.
- Competitor-B: offers aggressive quantization and edge-focused infra. Weakness: higher tail-latency when handling unpredictable bursts; harder to ensure consistent p95 at scale.
- Open-source self-hosting: theoretically cheaper at peak utilization, but ops cost + inability to auto-fallback leads to higher effective unit costs in real apps.

Sales demo snippets (30–60s soundbites):
- For product engineers: "We measure cost per meaningful token — with KV cache + batching you can cut effective token spend in half for multi-turn assistants. That means the same budget scales to roughly 2x the users."
- For infra/platform: "We guarantee predictable p95s via routing tiers and can fail over to lower-cost model variants automatically — so you avoid blackouts during traffic spikes."

Objection handling (concise):
- "Your numbers look optimistic" — reply: "Totally reasonable. We show both raw lab harness and a customer's anonymized profile with the same app pattern. Let's run a short PoC that's identical to your traffic shape."
- "Why not cheaper to self-host?" — reply: "Self-host can look cheap at 100% utilization, but production utilization is spiky; our batching+cache captures idle opportunities and we manage fallbacks and patching operationally — that’s where the unit-econ wins show up."

Proof artifacts to attach to demos (priority order):
1) Short video of lab run showing a burst and Redwood's stable p95 (30s clip).
2) CSV with p50/p95/p99 + cost-per-meaningful-token for two workload shapes.
3) One-pager end-to-end: what we measured, how, and configuration knobs used (batch sizes, cache TTLs, routing policy).

Quick config knobs to highlight in demos:
- Adaptive batching threshold and target latency SLO (demo toggle).
- Prefix/KV cache TTL and warming (show prewarmed vs cold run).
- Model-routing policy: prefer high-throughput slot then fallback to cheaper variant after X ms.

Metrics to use in customer conversations (avoid raw GPU jargon):
- User-facing: p95 latency, error rate, success rate (model fallback count).
- Economics: cost per 1k meaningful tokens, cost per 1k queries, expected monthly savings for given QPS profile.

Open questions / data needed before we externalize claims:
- Need 3 additional customer PoCs across different patterns (long-form generation, multi-turn chat, embeddings-heavy).
- Confirm numbers on the 13B family across both A100 and A10G infra (we have partials).
- Legal review on phrasing "2x lower" to ensure we include contestability language.

Next actions (owners & timeline):
- Rajiv: run two more lab runs with deterministic prompts and upload CSVs (due 2025-02-14).
- Maya: prepare a 1-page external claim brief with caution language for legal (due 2025-02-21).
- Connor: assemble demo clips and one-slide config toggles (due 2025-02-11).

Notes to field: keep claims tied to workload shape. When a buyer pushes for absolute numbers, move to: "we'll run a matched PoC against your traffic and show the delta."

Appendix (helpful phrases for emails / outreach):
- Subject line: "TCO and tail-latency improvements for production LLM apps"
- Opening line: "We help companies reduce tail-latency and per-meaningful-token spend by optimizing serving-level batching, cache, and routing — often cutting unit cost ~2x in production."
- CTA: "Quick PoC: we run your traffic for 48h and show p50/p95 and cost delta — no code changes required for the first pass."

Document history: created as a working GTM artifact to consolidate bench learnings and sales language. Expect iterative updates as more PoCs complete.
